qs.q:
Holidays — Which person…

A=Alison (Caribbean cruise; had to get visa at short notice; stressed at work; anticipates therapeutic benefits; everyone at office jealous)
B=Ben (Greek island villa; snap decision; steep villa price; magazine recommendation; self-catering; solo or group travellers)
C=Colin (safari in Namibia; won in magazine competition; many vaccinations; touring national park from base camp; worried about heat)
D=Deborah (canal barge every year; 4 mph, very relaxed; kingfishers and otters; overnight at pubs/marinas; laughter is the best medicine)
E=Ewan (all-inclusive package holiday; everything paid for; water park; nightlife; wife thinks no fun when everything handed to you)
F=Frances (Alps/Tyrol villa with neighbours; they wanted Rockies; demanding climbing; Derek takes photos; worried about clothing layers)

0. had always regretted not going somewhere? [A=Alison]
1. is going on the holiday they normally take?
2. is anticipating cold temperatures?
3. won their holiday in a competition?
4. considers their holiday the ultimate choice?
5. is surprised at the medical requirements for the holiday?
6. considers their holiday comparatively cheap?
7. is anxious about ascents?
8. only spent a short time considering their booking?
9. is taking a holiday on a small vessel?
10. is hoping the holiday will have medical benefits?
11. will stay in different places over the holiday?
12. is concerned about the food that will be available?
items: 1 — is going on the holiday they normally take?
3 — won their holiday in a competition?
4 — considers their holiday the ultimate choice?
5 — is surprised at the medical requirements for the holiday?
8 — only spent a short time considering their booking?
9 — is taking a holiday on a small vessel?
10 — is hoping the holiday will have medical benefits?
11 — will stay in different places over the holiday?
12 — is concerned about the food that will be available?

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"As students of architecture we used to refer to trees as GRACEFUL SUPPLEMENTS MAKING A HOUSE FEEL LIKE A HOME and ENRICHING THE VIEW FROM THE WINDOW."

Which statement about trees reflects Tom Baker's initial professional interest in trees?
A They remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
B They bring songbirds and wildlife close by.
C They make a neighbourhood more beautiful.
D They reduce the heat from streets and buildings.
opts: They remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
They bring songbirds and wildlife close by.
They make a neighbourhood more beautiful.
They reduce the heat from streets and buildings.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"After a local opinion poll, another interpretation has emerged, DEFINING THEM AS PLACES WHERE PEOPLE CAN INTERACT."

What are the benefits of more parks and green spaces, according to Brookson's residents?
A They reduce social isolation.
B They lower their carbon footprint.
C They produce habitats for many species.
D They present more opportunities for exercise.
opts: They produce habitats for many species.
They present more opportunities for exercise.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"City planners may PRIORITISE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE OVER GREEN SPACES... especially in HIGHLY URBANISED AREAS WHERE THERE IS LITTLE ROOM for property development."

Why are green spaces often not included in city planning?
A Because of the cities' low housing budgets.
B Because humans have changed them beyond return.
C Because people fail to realise how important green spaces are.
D Because in congested parts of the city space is in high demand.
opts: Because of the cities' low housing budgets.
Because humans have changed them beyond return.
Because people fail to realise how important green spaces are.
Because in congested parts of the city space is in high demand.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"We're currently promoting the latest data referring to the REDUCTION OF STRESS LEVELS AND ANXIETY."

Which slogan would summarise Tom's most recent campaign for making green spaces more popular?
A Green spaces remove pollutants.
B Green spaces improve mental health.
C Green spaces are educational and fun.
D Green spaces develop the identity of cities.
opts: Green spaces are educational and fun.
Green spaces develop the identity of cities.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"A solution may be creating MINI FORESTS IN THE SMALLER SPACES, growing up to 30 TIMES AS FAST as conventional ones."

How can green spaces be developed in urban areas?
A By employing rapid-growth techniques.
B By removing old buildings to insert green spaces.
C By letting existing green areas and natural forests grow.
D By planting numerous tree species to restore deteriorated land.
opts: By removing old buildings to insert green spaces.
By letting existing green areas and natural forests grow.
By planting numerous tree species to restore deteriorated land.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"MAINTAINING BIODIVERSITY for any green area is key for its own and HUMAN SURVIVAL in general."

In the last paragraph, what does Tom say should be given priority when planning a green space?
A The opinions and attitudes of the local population.
B The local government's plans for a particular area.
C The provision of habitats for local plant and animal species.
D The reduction of the environmental impact of life in city areas.
opts: The opinions and attitudes of the local population.
The local government's plans for a particular area.
The provision of habitats for local plant and animal species.
The reduction of the environmental impact of life in city areas.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"In general, labour markets have become less regulated and more insecure for workers. (19) ____. English has a word for it – 'downshifting' – signifying a career change to an activity perhaps less well paid, but offering better job satisfaction."

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Part of this trend is that professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades', as they were once dismissively termed.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system and have unexpected results.
F Many respondents reported being put off by the idea of a lifetime spent at a desk interacting with a computer screen.
G There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
